item.title: False King
item.description:
Overview

False King is a tactical roguelike deckbuilder set in a decaying royal court. You play as a disgraced advisor manipulating factions, forging alliances, and betraying rivals to place your chosen puppet on the throne. Every run rewrites the court’s history — and your deck.

My Role

As Systems Designer & Narrative Designer, I:

  • Designed the core Influence System — cards represent political leverage, not combat
  • Created the Faction Web — 6 noble houses with shifting alliances, secrets, and win conditions
  • Wrote the Branching Narrative — 50+ events with consequences that persist across runs
  • Built the Deckbuilding Loop — gain influence cards through intrigue, blackmail, favors
  • Prototyped in Godot with a focus on rapid iteration for systems balance

Key Features

  • Influence Deckbuilding — No HP or attack; cards are leverage (blackmail, favors, secrets, rumors)
  • Living Court — Factions remember your actions; betrayals have long-term consequences
  • Puppet Rulers — Choose your candidate; each has unique abilities and win conditions
  • Scandal Engine — Procedural events: affairs, embezzlement, assassinations, inheritances
  • Legacy Runs — Your choices unlock new puppets, factions, and court positions for future runs
  • Narrative Depth — 100+ written vignettes revealing the court’s rotting heart

Core Systems

Influence Mechanics

Card Types: Leverage | Secret | Favor | Rumor | Edict
Cost:      Influence Points (gained per turn)
Target:    Noble | Faction | Institution | The Throne
Effect:    Shift loyalty | Reveal info | Force action | Change rules

Faction Web

House Domain Win Condition Secret
Valoris Military Martial law Plotting coup
Meridius Commerce Trade monopoly Smuggling relics
Ombrelle Espionage Information control The King is dead
Solaine Religion Divine mandate Heretical texts
Ferrus Industry Resource control Forbidden alchemy
Vaelith Arcane Ritual completion Bound entity

Tech Stack

  • Engine: Godot 4.2 (GDScript)
  • Architecture: Event-driven with custom state machine for court simulation
  • Data: JSON/CSV for narrative content, ScriptableObject-like Resources for cards
  • Procedural: Markov chains for scandal generation, constraint solver for faction balance
  • Testing: Gut (Godot Unit Test) for system logic, headless simulation runs

Progress

  • ✅ Core influence card system
  • ✅ Faction simulation with loyalty/opinion
  • ✅ Basic run structure (court phases → events → resolution)
  • 🟡 Narrative content (30/100+ events written)
  • 🟡 Puppet ruler progression & unlocks
  • ⏳ UI/UX for deck management & court view
  • ⏳ Scandal engine & procedural events
  • ⏳ Visual style & VFX (tarot-card aesthetic)

Design Docs (Coming Soon)

  • Game Design Document — In progress
  • Influence System Design
  • Faction Web Architecture
  • Narrative Structure

item.title: False King — Game Design Document
item.description:
False King — Game Design Document

Status: Draft — Early design phase

High Concept

False King is a tactical roguelike deckbuilder where you manipulate a corrupted royal court through influence, secrets, and betrayal to place your chosen puppet on the throne. Your deck is not weapons — it’s leverage.

Core Pillars:

  1. Political Intrigue as Gameplay — Cards = leverage, not damage
  2. Emergent Narrative — Faction simulation creates unique stories each run
  3. Strategic Depth — Long-term planning across multiple court sessions

Core Gameplay Loop

[Choose Puppet] → [Court Session] → [Draw Influence Cards] → [Play Cards / Manipulate]
    ↓                                                              ↑
[Resolve Scandals] ← [Factions React] ← [Pass Turn / End Session]
    ↓
[Throne Check] → [Victory / Defeat / Next Session]
    ↓
[Legacy Unlocks] → [Next Run with New Options]

Systems Overview

Influence Card System

Card Type Cost Target Effect
Leverage 1-3 IP Noble Shift loyalty +10 to +30
Secret 2-4 IP Noble/Faction Reveal hidden trait/win condition
Favor 1-2 IP Noble Create debt → future discount
Rumor 1 IP Faction Shift public opinion
Edict 4-6 IP Institution Change court rules permanently

IP = Influence Points (3-5 per turn)
